title: Dispatch: suffocation recovery gate for characters (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (read it: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). Read first: AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0020 §§2-3; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts (rule:suffocating entry and ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS).

SOURCE (SRD rule:suffocating): "A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds). When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it can survive for a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 round). At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again."

SCOPE: CHARACTERS ONLY. The encounter-combatant dying state is a separate bead (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5); do not touch encounterCombatants.ts / update_combatant.

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0032_character_recovery_block.sql (the next contiguous number; follow ADR 0015 conventions used by 0020/0022, plain ALTER TABLE): add `character.recovery_block TEXT CHECK (recovery_block IS NULL OR recovery_block = 'suffocating')`. Update the schema.ts column-semantics comment.
2. state/hpLifecycle.ts gains two operations, each one transaction through the existing writeHpFields/mutateState path (so concentration breaks and provenance work as today):
   - `beginSuffocation(db, ctx)`: refuses a dead character; sets hp_current = 0, life_state = 'dying' (from alive, dying, or stable), resets both death-save counters when the character was not already dying, clears any stable-recovery deadline (writeHpFields already nulls it when not stable), and sets recovery_block = 'suffocating'. hp_temp is NOT changed: temporary hit points are not hit points (record this as a code comment citing the source wording). It is NOT damage: no overflow/instant death, no damage-at-0 failure, no concentration DC (leaving 'alive' breaks concentration as incapacitation via the existing hook). Calling it while already suffocating is an idempotent no-op that reports `alreadySuffocating: true`.
   - `endSuffocation(db, ctx, rng)`: refuses when no block is set; clears recovery_block. If the character is dying with death_save_successes = 3 (accrued while blocked, see 3), it becomes stable in the same transaction (counters reset, scheduleStableRecovery as stabilizeCharacter does).
3. While recovery_block is set:
   - applyHealing / any positive HP adjustment through adjustHp is refused with a MutateStateError naming the block ("cannot regain hit points while suffocating").
   - stabilizeCharacter is refused.
   - recordDeathSave: a natural 20 counts as one success (no HP regained); successes accumulate to at most 3 and a third success does NOT stabilize; failures and natural 1 behave as today (three failures kill). The result reports `recoveryBlocked: 'suffocating'`.
   - Every other path that raises hp_current or changes life_state toward alive/stable must respect the block: grep for hp_current writes (rest.ts short-rest hit-dice healing around the hit-dice spend, long-rest HP restoration, resolveStableRecoveries, grant paths). Refuse or skip with a clear error; never silently heal. Temporary HP grants are not hit points and stay allowed.
   - Death clears nothing special: a character that dies keeps no meaningful block; clear recovery_block when life_state becomes 'dead' (in writeHpFields or the transitions) so a dead row never carries it.
4. New tool `set_suffocation` (packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts, registered in tools.ts DEFAULT_TOOLS, mutates: true, follows toolStabilizeCharacter.ts patterns incl. CHARACTER_TARGET_SCHEMA): args { event: 'drop' | 'breathe', character? }. Description states only the contract: 'drop' applies the moment the rule drops the character to 0 hit points (dying, recovery blocked); 'breathe' records that it can breathe again; while blocked, healing and stabilize_character are refused and record_death_save does not stabilize or restore hit points; characters only. No arithmetic or timing recipe.
5. calc formulas in orchestrator/calc.ts (registry pattern of days_without_food_limit): `breath_hold_duration` → { minutes } = max(0.5, 1 + constitutionModifier) (0.5 = 30 seconds; return minutes as a number, plus `seconds`), and `suffocation_survival_rounds` → max(1, constitutionModifier). Each cites SRD rule:suffocating in its comment like the others. Add calc.test.ts cases incl. the source example (Con 14 → +2 → 3 minutes; 2 rounds) and minimums.
6. Update tool descriptions truthfully: record_death_save (blocked behaviour), stabilize_character (refused while suffocating), adjust_hp (healing refused while suffocating). Keep existing sentences otherwise; do not add per-rule prose.
7. Known limit (ruleKnownLimits.ts) rule:suffocating: re-derive under R0. The CHARACTER clause is now executable: rewrite that part to the bounded trap/path statement (e.g. a character whose breath runs out is dropped with set_suffocation event drop at the start of its turn, and event breathe when it can breathe again; durations come from calc breath_hold_duration and suffocation_survival_rounds). Remove 'suffocation-recovery-gate' from this limit's capabilityGaps and from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS. KEEP the encounter-combatant sentence and the 'combatant-dying-state' gap unchanged. participants must list every tool named and each must appear in the statement (validator). Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts and the suffocation statement tests there and in tools.test.ts (the old 'record_death_save is not gated' / 'do not call stabilize_character' wording assertions must be replaced by assertions on the new contract, not deleted without replacement). The 8-word source-restatement test in ruleDispositions.test.ts must stay green.
8. Design doc: in docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md A5 classification table, move the suffocation-recovery-gate cell to landed (one short note: "landed in eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4"). Do not rewrite other text.

TESTS (permanent evidence, generalized not per-wording): hpLifecycle.test.ts: beginSuffocation from alive/stable/dying; refused on dead; temp HP untouched; concentration broken from alive; healing refused while blocked; stabilize refused; nat 20 = one success no HP; third success does not stabilize; three failures kill and clear the block; endSuffocation with 3 successes stabilizes and arms recovery; endSuffocation with <3 leaves dying; every other HP-regain path you gated has a refusal test. A tool-registry test invoking set_suffocation end to end. Migration test pattern as used for 0020 if one exists.

OUT OF SCOPE: combatants; the countdown itself (no timer state); any other rule.

SCHEMA SNAPSHOT: if a committed schema snapshot/migration test exists (see packages/core/scripts/generate-schema-snapshot.ts and `npm -w @eshyra/core run schema:snapshot`), regenerate it through that script; never hand-edit it.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation per the description on branch <child-id>; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the child.

Dispatched 2026-10-02 gpt-6-luna effort high, pgid 2353123, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4.1 off eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8@18c1b305.
Implemented character suffocation recovery gate and committed as 6daab44b on eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4.1.

Files changed: added migration 0032 and regenerated schema snapshot; extended hpLifecycle/mutateState and level-up guard; added set_suffocation and calc formulas; updated tool descriptions, rule known-limit statement/gap registry, A5 classification row, and migration/tool/rules/lifecycle/rest/calc/concentration tests.

Decisions: followed the dispatched design. Suffocation enters through the existing HP write path, retaining temporary HP while dropping current HP to zero; healing and stabilization are blocked, death saves preserve progress without recovery, and breathing clears the block and resolves three successes to stable. Rest recovery uses the guarded adjustHp path; level-up projections reject the block. No code-forced design deviations. No discovered follow-up beads.

Evidence: npm run verify:worktree passed after final edits: 317 test files passed, 2 skipped; 5,590 tests passed, 3 skipped. This included format, hidden-Unicode check, lint, full typecheck, and full test suite. git diff --check passed; working tree clean after commit.
